
### ARP/ND protocols  {.smaller}


* filling in tables dynamically?
* key idea: ask <i>everyone</i> on network
* entity with that IP address responds 
<hr class="vspace" />
* IPv4: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP)
* IPv6: ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery (ND) 

   * ICMP = Internet Control Message Protocol



### ARP messages  {.smaller}


* suppose router IP address 10.0.2.15 and MAC address 02:…:DE needs to find out that 10.0.2.2 uses 03:…:EE 
<hr class="vspace" />
* 02:…:DE→FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF: request 10.0.2.2 <br> tell 10.0.2.15 (=02:…:DE) 

   * FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF = broadcast (send to all on network)

* 03:…:EE→02:…:DE: reply 10.0.2.2=03:…:EE <br> tell 10.0.2.15=02:…:DE

### ARP messages (revisited)  {.smaller}


* suppose router IP address 10.0.2.15 and MAC address 02:…:DE needs to find out that 10.0.2.2 uses 03:…:EE 
<hr class="vspace" />
* 02:…:DE$\rightarrow$FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF: request 10.0.2.2 <br> tell 10.0.2.15 (=02:…:DE) 

   * <em>everyone who receives this can add 10.0.2.15=02:…:DE to neighbor table</em>

* 03:…:EE$\rightarrow$02:…:DE: reply 10.0.2.2=03:…:EE <br> tell 10.0.2.15=02:…:DE 

   * <em>everyone who receives this can add 10.0.2.2=03:…:EE to neighbor table</em>



### ICMPv6 ND  {.smaller}


* IPv6 uses different protocol for this
* … but mostly works the same 
<hr class="vspace" />
* differences:
* sent as IPv6 packets
* requests sent to special multicast address 

   * goal: allow nodes to easily ignore irrelevant requests

* different names: 

   * request = solicitiation
   * reply = advertisement
